_about: Packet 2.91 (V056). One diagram decision per chapter for the five sections packet 2.9 pinned that carry diagrams (published 25 September 2026, 12:11 UTC, so these apply to LIVE content). `diagram` is the id the check-in must show; null means the chapter was read and teaches none of the section's diagrams, so it shows none (decidedNoDiagram). Chosen by reading each chapter (audit/runs/packet-2.9/sections/<id>.txt) under the rule 2.9 used for questions: a chapter shows a diagram only if it TEACHES what the diagram draws. Then judged by a blind second reader (blind-verdicts.json: a Sonnet reader given only the chapter text and the diagram list, not these choices). It agreed on 10 of 13 first readings; the three that moved carry `firstReading` and say why. All 13 final decisions are the blind reader's `best`.

government-intervention-firms.title: Competition Policy
government-intervention-firms.why: CMA, merger control and cartels. None of the three diagrams is taught here; privatisation is chapter 2.

government-intervention-firms.title: Government Failure and Minimum Wages
government-intervention-firms.why: Teaches the minimum wage in a monopsony labour market. Unchanged.

growth-development.title: Growth vs Development
growth-development.why: Teaches the HDI's three dimensions as the measure that separates development from growth, which is the chapter's title. Harrod-Domar and Prebisch-Singer are taught here too (Barriers to Development). The blind reader chose HDI; the first reading kept the served Harrod-Domar only because it was not wrong, and HDI was otherwise shown nowhere in Learn Mode.

growth-development.title: Development Strategies
growth-development.why: Teaches market-led against interventionist strategies. Unchanged.

growth-development.title: Sustainability
growth-development.why: Sustainable development and green growth. None of the five diagrams is taught here.

labour-markets.title: Demand and Supply of Labour
labour-markets.why: Teaches labour demand (MRP) and labour supply SEPARATELY; the equilibrium where DL = SL, which is what the served 'Competitive Labour Market Equilibrium' draws, is taught in chapter 2 ('Competitive Labour Markets'). The blind reader found it; the first reading had accepted it on the MRP-shift sentence. It is the V056 shape exactly: a diagram one chapter early.

labour-markets.title: Wage Determination
labour-markets.why: Teaches monopsony: MCL above supply, hire at MCL = MRP, and the minimum wage. The diagram was unplaced and the chapter showed none.

labour-markets.title: Trade Unions and Wage Differentials
labour-markets.why: Teaches wage differentials and labour immobility. Unchanged.

poverty-inequality.title: Types of Poverty
poverty-inequality.why: Teaches the Lorenz curve and the Gini coefficient (A / (A+B)) in its second subsection, immediately before the check-in; absolute against relative poverty is taught too. The blind reader chose the Lorenz curve; it is the diagram a student is asked to draw, and it was otherwise shown nowhere in Learn Mode.

poverty-inequality.title: Causes and Consequences
poverty-inequality.why: Causes of inequality and redistribution. The Kuznets curve is taught nowhere in the section, and the Lorenz curve is chapter 1's.

role-state-macroeconomy.title: Market Failure and the State
role-state-macroeconomy.why: Public goods and goods with external benefits. It served Crowding Out in the Loanable Funds Market, on the word 'market'; crowding out is taught nowhere in the section.

role-state-macroeconomy.title: Macroeconomic Policy
role-state-macroeconomy.why: Teaches fiscal and monetary policy shifting AD and supply-side policy shifting LRAS. Unchanged.
